clue.text: A delicate pregnant lady's clothing displayed with skill

indicators.note: the clothing of a word is its outside letters, so each of these words gives only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A dainty expectant mother shows off her maternity wear with flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' takes the outer letters DE, PT and LY from delicate, pregnant and lady; the 's on lady's is just a link, and 'displayed' joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something adeptly means doing it expertly, which is a plain synonym of acting with skill.

clue.text: Active promotion for several in police department

indicators.note: promotion means going up, which in a down answer reads the letters bottom to top
in puts several inside the police department

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
many means several

explanation.surface: A lively promotion for several officers in the police department.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'promotion' means going up, so the letters are read from bottom to top; CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dynamic is energetic and full of action, so is active.

clue.text: Drop of wine

definitions.meaning: to drop something heavily is to put it down with a thud

explanation.definitionFit: Plonk means both setting down heavily and, in British slang, cheap wine.

clue.text: In future, a left side

parts.note: later means at a future time

explanation.surface: A forecast that one day there will be a left wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Lateral describes something at or toward the side, so the word relates to a side.

clue.text: Aroma produced by each 12 not right

parts.note: per means each, as in 'a pound per person'

indicators.note: not right asks for the letter standing for right to be removed

parts.note: the answer to 12 across is a smoker; a fumer is one who gives off smoke

explanation.surface: A smell given off by every cigarette smoker, minus one: a cryptic sum about tobacco odour.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 12 across, SMOKER, which must be replaced by the synonym FUMER before 'not right' drops its R.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfume is a pleasant scent, so it is a kind of aroma.

clue.text: Old Testament character's describing New Testament incidents

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around something, so these letters encircle the next piece

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in Genesis, plus the possessive S

explanation.surface: An Old Testament figure narrating episodes from the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing a line around something, not telling about it.
explanation.definitionFit: Events are things that happen, and incidents are individual happenings, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Devotee separately wrapping partner and himself in the middle? That's extraordinary

indicators.note: separately says the devotee takes in the second letter at a different point from the first
wrapping says the devotee goes round the letters that follow

parts.note: a fanatic is a devoted enthusiast

indicators.note: in, read with the middle that follows, asks for the central letter of the partner word
the middle asks for the central letter of this seven-letter word

explanation.surface: A fan who wraps both a partner and himself in the middle: a striking feat.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters T and S go into FANATIC separately: FAN-T-A-S-TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic in everyday speech means remarkable or wonderful, just as extraordinary does.

clue.text: Staff get on with right boss

parts.note: to man a post is to staff it
to age is to get on in years

explanation.surface: Staff getting along with a right-wing boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' and 'get on' are verbs here: MAN and AGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A manager runs a team, which is what a boss does.

clue.text: Put off one speech in decline

parts.note: to deter is to put off or discourage
I is the Roman numeral one
an oration is a formal speech

explanation.surface: Postponing a speech while one's health is failing.
explanation.definitionFit: Deterioration is a worsening over time, which is a decline in quality or condition.

clue.text: Finally, you can afford to disengage

indicators.note: finally asks for the closing letter of each of the following words in turn

explanation.surface: At last you have the money to pull out of a commitment.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a catch or fastening is to release or disengage it.

clue.text: So few into heritage plan renovated a listed building

definitions.note: listed puns on 'leaning to one side' as well as 'officially protected'

indicators.note: renovated means made over, so the letters of these words are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: A heritage scheme that puts little money into restoring a protected building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Listed' in Britain means a building protected for its historic interest; here it also means tilting, which fits the famous tower exactly.
explanation.definitionFit: The tilting bell tower in the Italian city is both heritage-protected and literally listing, so it is a listed building in two senses.

clue.text: One has a habit that might be irksome, but not I

definitions.note: a person with a regular tobacco habit

indicators.note: might be suggests the letters could form something else once rearranged
but not tells us one letter of the fodder is left out of the shuffle

explanation.surface: Someone with an irritating personal habit, unlike the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might be' shuffles IRKSOME, and 'but not' removes its I before the shuffle; the habit is the cigarette habit the clue hints is irksome to others.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who smokes regularly has a nicotine habit, so is a person with a habit.

clue.text: Alienate and upset sergeant

indicators.note: upset means knocked over or disturbed, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: An instruction to alienate an army sergeant and make him cross.
explanation.definitionFit: To estrange someone is to drive them away emotionally, the same as to alienate.

clue.text: Youngster to lose control round hotel in fashionable setting

indicators.note: round means the first piece goes around what follows

parts.note: a car that skids loses control

indicators.note: in puts the hotel letter within the next piece
setting means the fashionable word acts as the frame holding the hotel letter

parts.note: cool means fashionable
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A young person about to lose their temper in a trendy hotel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lose control' is a verb phrase for a car sliding, and 'hotel' is a single NATO alphabet letter rather than a building in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A child at school is a youngster, so the compound is simply a young pupil.

clue.text: Choice over time of surgery

indicators.note: over means the choice word is laid across the time word, covering it

parts.note: an option is a choice
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A patient choosing the time of their surgery.
explanation.definitionFit: An operation is a surgical procedure, which is what surgery means here.

clue.text: Isn't Rob Roy featured regularly in this narrative?

indicators.note: featured regularly asks for every other letter of these words, starting with the second

explanation.surface: A question about whether the outlaw hero Rob Roy appears in a tale.
explanation.walkthrough: Rob Roy is the Scottish outlaw of Walter Scott's novel, which makes 'narrative' feel like a book reference.
explanation.definitionFit: A story is an account of events, which is what a narrative is.

clue.text: See 11
Where to grow fruit or veg

parts.note: chard is a leafy vegetable

explanation.surface: A gardener asking where to grow fruit or vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchard is a plot planted with fruit trees, a place for growing fruit.

clue.text: Not a subject to knock back in Somerset: a cider press

indicators.note: knock back says the hidden letters are read backwards
in means the answer lies inside these words, running across their boundaries

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Knocking back drink at a Somerset cider press, the county being famous for cider.
explanation.walkthrough: Somerset is an English county known for cider. 'knock back' sounds like drinking, but it reverses the letters found in 'Somerset: a cider press'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar a sentence splits into subject and predicate, so the predicate is the part that is not the subject.

clue.text: Picture designer with a degree

parts.note: Christian Dior was a famous fashion designer
MA is a Master of Arts degree

explanation.surface: A portrait of a designer who holds a degree.
explanation.definitionFit: A diorama is a three-dimensional scene or model, a kind of picture.

clue.text: Posed, clothing reduced, up for minimal cover

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the letters are read from the bottom
clothing means the posed word wraps round the reduced word

parts.note: sat means posed, as for a portrait
less means reduced

explanation.surface: A model posing for a portrait with less and less on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses the whole assembly because this is a down entry; 'clothing' is a containment signal, though the surface makes it about garments.
explanation.definitionFit: Tassels on a burlesque costume cover the barest minimum, so they are minimal cover.

clue.text: Sleep with soldier, putting head down for a sausage?

indicators.note: putting head down means the first letter drops to the bottom of the down entry

parts.note: shag is British slang for having sex with someone
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier sleeping around, with a rude crossword twist.
explanation.walkthrough: SHAG + GI makes SHAGGI; its head S moves to the bottom. A haggis is the Scottish dish of offal in a casing, hence the question mark on 'sausage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A haggis is offal stuffed into a stomach casing, which makes it a sausage of sorts.

clue.text: Cousteau, perhaps, has an alternative for us

definitions.text: Cousteau, perhaps, has an alternative for us

indicators.note: perhaps hints the name's letters could be arranged otherwise
an alternative for one thing replaces it, so one pair of letters takes the place of another

explanation.surface: A remark that the famous diver Cousteau offers something different for the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: In COUSTEAU swap US for AN, giving COANTEAU, and rearrange those letters ('perhaps'); the name also serves as the example in the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Cousteau was a pioneering undersea explorer, an example of a deep-sea diver or oceanaut.

clue.text: See 11
Like a man from Spain, but without his fear

indicators.note: without asks for the following word to be taken out

parts.note: Hispanic describes someone of Spanish origin

explanation.surface: A Spaniard who is fearless.
explanation.definitionFit: Panic is sudden overwhelming fear, so it is a strong form of fear.

clue.text: What raises family is covered by "for a start, be a good sport and fuss around!"

indicators.note: is covered by means the family word sits inside the letters that follow
for a start asks for the opening letter of each of the next words

parts.note: kin means family

indicators.note: around turns the fuss word back to front

parts.note: ado is fuss, as in much ado about nothing

explanation.surface: A family pep talk urging someone to be a sport and fuss around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What raises' looks like the start of a sentence but is the definition: something that makes a cake rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Bicarbonate of soda is a leavening agent that makes cakes rise, so it is something that raises dough.

clue.text: Want to handle dough while talking

indicators.note: while talking means the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: to knead is to work dough with the hands

explanation.surface: Wanting to handle money while chatting, dough being slang for cash.
explanation.walkthrough: Dough looks like slang for money; here it is bread dough.
explanation.definitionFit: To need something is to lack and require it, which is to want it in the older sense.

clue.text: Ministers send documents back, showing eccentricity

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
showing means the answer is on display within these words, spanning their boundaries

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Government ministers returning paperwork in a strange way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' signals letters on display within 'Ministers send documents', and 'back' reads that run, SSENDDO, backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Oddness is strangeness of behaviour, which is what eccentricity describes.

clue.text: So returning in the grip of tight authoritarian

indicators.note: in the grip of means the first piece is held inside the tight word

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed, tight

indicators.note: returning means the Latin word is read backwards

parts.note: sic is Latin for so or thus, as used in quotations

explanation.surface: A tight-fisted dictator returning to power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So' is the Latin sic, the word editors put in brackets to mean 'thus, as written'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fascist supports a dictatorial, authoritarian regime, so the words are near synonyms.
